control_implications.significance: A hypervisor memory isolation failure allowed cross-VM data access on shared cloud infrastructure. control_implications.headline: GPGME library memory bug affects all dependent applications
control_implications.significance: A critical memory corruption in the widely used GPGME library puts all dependent applications at risk until upgraded. Vulnerability management owners should inventory software using GPGME and verify that version 2.3.0 or later has been deployed across the estate.

control_implications.significance: A ransomware recovery provider was found to be paying attackers rather than decrypting data, misleading victims. paragraphs.text: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including critical flaws in VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller, and SAP NetWeaver. A China-linked group exploited a VMware vCenter zero-day for authentication bypass in September 2026. Attackers compromised Cisco Expressway devices within days of proof-of-concept publication. These events demand immediate vulnerability management review across affected platforms.

A Linux KVM hypervisor flaw enables cross-VM memory access on AMD hosts with nested virtualization, exposing tenant data on shared cloud infrastructure. The GPGME cryptographic library contains a critical memory bug affecting all dependent applications prior to version 2.3.0. A ransomware recovery service operator was indicted for wire fraud after paying attackers instead of decrypting victim data. These developments affect data protection, software supply chain integrity, and third-party risk assurance.
